observations: Damage: Root inspected all 45 fresh damage images through eight contact sheets and the EXP recovered roof, Jeep object impact, dirt-mud transition and both garage-state originals at full 1600x900 resolution. All nine bodies show local front deformation after actual repeated wall impacts; their Free Run counterparts are clean.

Damage: Observed inverted landings and recovered roof views retain readable paint, glass, lamp materials and original wheel/underbody hardware. The EXP solar faces, grid and white cap follow the dent together without the earlier white intersection through the panels.

Damage: All seven enabled-damage transition captures show continuous textured ground and surface-appropriate marks. The dirt-mud capture no longer has the pale sky hole seen in rejected candidates; the paired native coverage and momentum checks also pass. These finite views do not establish every frame or terrain location.

Damage: The garage DAMAGE ON state visibly reports Condition 28%, drive 38%, brakes 68% and two impacts; Free Run visibly reports damage off and a clean vehicle. Repair and mode controls fit without overlapping the vehicle tabs or footer.

Damage: Deformation remains bounded surface damage with gameplay drive/brake/steering effects and intact original collision hulls. No detached parts or full structural collapse is inferred from these captures, and the first accepted impact still has a one-time CPU preparation cost.

ElectricPressure: Root inspected all 36 fresh electric/pressure captures through six contact sheets and all three upgrade-row originals at full 1600x900. Native vehicle selections and converted-body views retain their materials, tire contact and repaired Free Run appearance without a new visual import defect.

ElectricPressure: The actual G580 MOTOR POWER page clearly retains Factory 4 motor EV and displays +40% output / 811 hp for stage II. Its ICE CONVERSION page displays STOCK, 350HP, 500HP and 700HP, with the fitted 500 hp V8 / eight-speed and -1019 lb estimated conversion mass. Selected rows fit completely within the scroll viewport and remain above the damage/repair footer.

ElectricPressure: The actual Civic EV CONVERSION page displays STOCK, SINGLE, DUAL and QUAD with the selected dual kit reporting two motors, 268 hp, 80 kWh and AWD HIGH. Factory-EV gasoline conversion choices and factory-combustion EV swap choices are visibly distinct.

ElectricPressure: The paired road braking/steering and sand captures show supported tires and surface-appropriate markings; black marks occur on paved trials and the sand comparison retains textured soft ground. The numerical corridor, pressure, independent wheel-channel and finite-rate air-control checks provide the dynamic evidence beyond these static views.

ElectricPressure: Conversion outputs, component masses and tire behavior remain simulator estimates rather than manufacturer retrofit offerings or tire ratings. These images and actual Slate attribute checks do not claim a separate mouse-click or controller driving session.

Mechanical: Root inspected all 18 fresh front-facing stock/portal garage captures in three contact sheets, covering all nine vehicles. Bodies, separate tire/rim assemblies, lamps and visible underbody parts remain connected without an obvious missing mesh or material regression.

Mechanical: Paired portal selections show the fitted vehicle states and increased running weights while retaining each vehicle's recognizable body and wheel scale. The captured garage footer and Free Run controls remain readable and separate from the vehicle and scrolling information card.

Mechanical: The 500 native mechanical assertions supply the detailed moving axle, steering, brake, rotor, wheel and portal alignment evidence. These overview captures do not independently resolve every small mechanical joint or demonstrate a manual driving session.

Art: Root inspected all 90 fresh native images in 15 six-image contact sheets and both Mercedes front, side and elevated front-quarter originals at 1600x900. The six preserved other bodies retain their recognizable silhouettes, trim, glass, separate tires/rims and lamp roles without a new missing-body or material regression.

Art: The cooked G580 and G63 show the corrected circular headlight size and spacing, narrower variant grilles, shallow roof edge, rounded actual window openings and a simple descending hood/wing seam. Side views retain the measured wheelbase and distinguish the G580 20-inch wheel/tire combination from the G63 selected 22-inch forged wheels.

Art: The EV's raised softer bonnet, aerodynamic trim, Black Panel outline and rear Design Box distinguish it from the AMG grille, covered spare and side exhausts. No folded fascia triangles or painted closure over the glass appeared in the inspected views.
Art: The EXP cap and solar assembly are intact in the clean model views after offline refinement. Damage-time separation still belongs to the dedicated damage review.

Art: These remain photo/drawing-based procedural reconstructions. Door and quarter sheets, mirrors/handles, bumper inserts and cabins are simplified; the AMG hood reflections are softer and blunter than the manufacturer's pressed sheet. Static view approval does not establish OEM CAD or production racing-game fidelity.

Full: Root inspected all 25 fresh Full captures in five contact sheets and the actual driven-snow original at 1280x720. All nine coachwork bodies remain rendered above the quarry surface with readable paint, glazing, tires/rims and variant fittings; no new missing body, transparent terrain or obvious burial appears in these banked-support captures.

Full: The six driven soil captures distinguish a light hard-dirt trail, darker mud/wetland grooves, shallow sand disturbance, compressed pale-blue snow tread and exposed soft-dirt paths. The snow original has tread relief, continuous shoulder shading and no black rubber ribbon or sky opening; the crushed-grass view shows low bent plants along the driven line.

Full: The six Urus hero views retain its bonnet relief, open intakes, sloping glazing, rear hatch treatment and separate wheels. They remain simplified procedural surfaces and interiors. Acceleration and differential-lock captures show the actual HUD/vehicle states, but a static frame alone does not prove route completion; that is established by the fresh 344 passing native assertions.

The seven boundary frames show continuous ground under the moving Jeep, distinct graded surface materials and appropriate disturbed tire paths. No pale sky rectangle appears in the dirt-mud capture.

The HUMMER original shows the body above the tarmac with its wheels still exposed; these rear camera views do not resolve every suspension joint or establish exact compression by appearance alone.

Very dark square-ended pavement strips remain visible in the suspension-rise frames, and distant vegetation and terrain repetition remain cosmetic limitations.

No newly absent geometry, sky hole or obvious material/shadow failure appears across the three views.

Presets: The car is partly cropped by the established elevated review camera in each image. Terrain saturation, plant repetition and simplified coachwork remain visible and are not hidden by the preset comparison. Real-time quarry throughput is assessed separately from these brief configuration/render checks.

None of these inspected poses shows the deep body burial from the reported stuck-Sprinter screenshot. These clean-body rollover fixtures use Free Run so deliberate impacts do not contaminate the separate visible-damage acceptance.

Ruts: Root inspected all16 fresh rut PNGs in three contact sheets. Mud and wet-grass cases show brown grooves with physically shaded shoulders; snow shows pale compressed tread and raised/shaded edges. The driven mud and snow trials produce continuous paired grooves behind the moving Jeep without visible sky holes.

Ruts: Firm dirt, sand and loose-dirt disturbance is much shallower and less contrasted than the mud grooves. The low sand profile is particularly subtle in these frames. These are bounded simulation profiles, not an assertion of large terrain excavation or photoreal soil displacement.

Ruts: All117 native checks pass for physical depression, displaced/compacted volumes, shoulders, persistence and actual driven mud/snow contact. No black pavement ribbon is visible on these soil surfaces. Tread cadence, parallel edges and vegetation repetition remain visibly regular.

The gravel original retains complete textured ground and the clean vehicle, but very small ejected fragments are difficult to distinguish from scattered ground stones.

Spray: All44 native debris checks pass for surface-dependent emitted types, nonstatic trajectory evolution and bounded lifetime/contact behavior. These numerical checks establish motion that a still capture cannot. No terrain sky hole, missing vehicle body or obvious material failure appears in the inspected views.

Spray: Visible fragments remain simplified small instanced forms. This review does not establish realistic high-density dust, splashes or a continuous cinematic spray effect; it verifies the existing bounded surface-dependent implementation against the current package.

Transitions: Root inspected all14 fresh transition PNGs in three contact sheets. The two views of each of seven boundaries retain continuous textured ground, distinct terrain interiors and irregular graded edges. No pale sky rectangle is visible at the dirt-mud boundary or elsewhere in these inspected captures.

Transitions: The yellow-green meadow fringe is still overly uniform in places, and distant plant spacing, low-detail rocks and repeated ground detail remain visible.
